Acute Medicine – Discharge Summary

Discharge Summary

Admission date/time: 12:21 on 11/03/2020
Discharge date/time: 21:57 on 01/04/2020

Presenting complaint: Fever, cough and breathlessness with hypoxia (SpO2 <92% on
recorded 06:52 on 11/03/2020).

Diagnosis: COVID-19 pneumonitis, confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR (swab taken 10:36
on 11/03/2020, positive result reported 21:50 on 11/03/2020).

Hospital course: Admitted to the acute medical unit for oxygen therapy and monitoring. VTE
thromboprophylaxis with enoxaparin was commenced, first dose given 07:38 on 13/03/2020
following a brief delay due to ward stock shortage. Oxygen requirement peaked at 4L via
nasal cannula in the first week, with gradual improvement over the following two weeks.
Remained on the ward throughout and did not require critical care input. Course complicated
by prolonged fatigue and deconditioning requiring extended physiotherapy prior to
discharge. Inflammatory markers tended down; renal function remained normal throughout.

Medications on discharge: Enoxaparin continued for a further two weeks post-discharge for
extended VTE prophylaxis given prolonged immobility. Regular paracetamol continued as
required. Usual antihypertensive medication resumed unchanged.

Follow-up arrangements: Respiratory clinic review arranged within 2 weeks of discharge to
assess recovery and consider need for further imaging.

GP actions: Please continue the extended enoxaparin course as prescribed and monitor for
signs of bleeding. Please arrange follow-up bloods (FBC, U&E) one week after discharge and
review medication compliance. Advise gradual return to activity and urgent review if
breathlessness worsens.
